evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The `manager_restarted` predicate only checks that both manager PIDs are positive and differ, and that both invocation IDs are present and differ. It never checks that the two manager snapshots are from the same boot. A guest reboot between the two observations changes both the manager PID and invocation ID, so the predicate would report an isolated manager restart even though the observations span a reboot. The reboot snapshots already carry `boot_id`, so the smallest fix is to also require nonempty, equal manager-snapshot boot IDs while retaining the PID and invocation-ID comparisons.
